title: Copenhagen February 27 Men in Black protest against extended Covid restrictions

location.site: Copenhagen; crowd reported at the square in front of City Hall by evening

participants_original: Police report via AFP/The Local: around 600 initially, swelling to around 1,200 by the end of the evening at the square in front of Copenhagen City Hall.
threshold_50_evidence: Police-reported estimates are around 600 initially and around 1,200 later, both well above 50; these are approximate time-specific estimates, not bounds or independent counts.

start_date.summary: The article identifies Saturday, February 27, 2021, as the executed Copenhagen gathering.

location.summary: Copenhagen is named; the article places the growing late-evening crowd at the square in front of City Hall but does not establish where the gathering began.

organizer.summary: The Local body identifies the group calling itself Men in Black as organizer.

demands.summary: The protest followed the government's extension of many coronavirus restrictions; the rally is described as anti-lockdown.

participants.summary: Police estimates reported via AFP/The Local: around 600 initially and around 1,200 by late evening; retain wording and do not infer exact minimum/maximum bounds.

protester_violence.summary: Police described the demonstration as largely peaceful but reported arrests for alleged fireworks use and rowdy behavior without specifying target or act; violence classification remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Eight arrests are reported. No beating, dispersal, accommodation, ignoring, shooting or killing response is established in the public text read.

end_date.summary: The report's late-evening crowd estimate does not establish when the physical gathering ended.

notes: Body read was limited to the public text at lines 125–171; the page reached a login prompt at line 173. No login or paywall access was attempted, and images/embedded posts were not assessed. S006 and S007 are search-only Euronews AFP translations/republications and are not independent corroboration. The eight arrests are response arrests, not turnout; fireworks and rowdy-behavior allegations do not alone establish protester violence or crowd dispersal. The reported policy announcement is context, not evidence of a concession or completed state response. Distinct from February 6 and January MIB actions; broader campaign boundary remains unresolved.
open_questions: Establish physical gathering end and any operational police dispersal; do not infer either from the late-evening attendance estimate or arrests.
Verify what the alleged fireworks and rowdy behavior involved and whether any acts were directed at state personnel/property.
Review continuity with the February 6 event and January gatherings under the missing detailed procedure; do not merge on organizer name alone.
Check whether government action after the rally was responsive to participants, rather than relying on policy announcements already reported as preceding the event.
